subject: Read the taskq queue from disk so the panel shows what the transcript cannot
description:
The task panel reconstructs taskq tasks from the transcript alone: the id from the record, the description from the command line. Both halves can be missing in practice. A description built in a shell variable is unrecoverable (v1.119.0 makes that honest by recording nothing rather than the literal dollar-D), a heredoc or command substitution is gone entirely, and a record read past a resume point has no create at all.

But the queue is a FILE STORE, and the truth is sitting on disk: tasks/*.json at the git root of the session cwd, with the full subject, description, status, owner and blockers.

engine/tasks.rs already has the pattern -- see the merge doc comment: "Merge the live on-disk state over the op-log reconstruction: disk wins per task id (it is the queue current truth and carries full detail); op-log items fill in for pruned/gc-d files." That is written for the harness own task sidecar. Point the same mechanism at the taskq store and every gap above closes at once.

Sketch: resolve the session cwd to a git root, read tasks/*.json there (task_from_json is already on the seam), merge over the op-log list with disk winning per id. Guard it: a session whose cwd no longer exists, a repo whose queue belongs to different work, and the cost of stat-ing a directory on every fold.

NOTE for whoever picks this up: pass --description as a LITERAL, never as a shell variable. The viewer reads the command line, so "$D" records nothing. This very task was first filed that way, which is a fair demonstration of the bug it describes.

Definition of done: a session that ran taskq shows every task with its real description regardless of how the command was written; a session with no queue is unchanged; the byte-identical gate re-baselined for the panel rows that gain text.
activeForm: Merging the taskq store into the task panel
